gloss: to approach; to come near; to draw close

definitions.gloss: to approach; to come near; to draw close
definitions.explanation: To move physically closer to someone or something. Can also be used figuratively for approaching a topic or person emotionally. An intransitive godan verb with the ～に particle marking the target.

examples.japanese: {猫|ねこ}がそっと{近寄|ちかよ}ってきた。
あの{建物|たてもの}には{近寄|ちかよ}らないほうがいい。
examples.english: You'd better not go near that building.

examples.japanese: {見知|みし}らぬ{人|ひと}が{近寄|ちかよ}ってきたので、{少|すこ}し{警戒|けいかい}した。
examples.english: A stranger approached me, so I became a little wary.

notes:
USAGE:
The target of approach is marked with に: ～に{近寄|ちかよ}る. Often appears with ～てくる to indicate approaching the speaker, or ～ていく for moving away from the speaker toward something.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～に{近寄|ちかよ}る (to approach ~)
- {近寄|ちかよ}ってくる (to come closer — toward speaker)
- {近寄|ちかよ}らないでください (please don't come near)
- {近寄|ちかよ}りがたい (unapproachable, intimidating)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{近|ちか}づく is very similar and often interchangeable, but {近寄|ちかよ}る tends to emphasize deliberate physical movement toward a target, while {近|ちか}づく can also describe things becoming closer in time or abstract distance.
